name: Stop the diagnostic tracking services
summary: Turn off the services that collect and forward diagnostic data.
what: Sets the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service (DiagTrack) and the WAP push message routing service (dmwappushservice) to Disabled and stops them.
benefit: Removes the background process that gathers and uploads diagnostic data.
risk: Low. Some feedback and diagnostic features report less. Windows Update is not affected.
advice: Suggested if you want the collector off. Skip it if you use Insider builds or send feedback often.
facts: DiagTrack is the Connected User Experiences and Telemetry service
dmwappushservice routes push messages used by diagnostics
None of the privacy settings turn off Windows Update
Windows may turn them back on after a big update and Clarion will flag it

name: Turn off diagnostic scheduled tasks
summary: Disable the scheduled jobs that gather app and usage data.
what: Disables the Compatibility Appraiser, Program Data Updater, Consolidator and USB CEIP tasks.
benefit: Stops periodic data collection jobs and the CPU and disk bursts they cause.
risk: Low. Feature updates may take slightly longer to check app compatibility.
advice: Suggested if you want fewer background jobs. Safe to skip.
facts: Covers four tasks: Compatibility Appraiser, ProgramDataUpdater, Consolidator and UsbCeip
Tasks missing on your build are skipped
Stops periodic scans that cause short CPU and disk bursts
